\title{Guardrails for the Record Race: What a CsPbI3 Cell Can Honestly Claim (24.9\% $\rightarrow$ 20.8\%)}
\author{Hussain Touhid Siddiquee\thanks{Department of EEE, Leading University, Sylhet-3112, Bangladesh. E-mail: touhidsiddiqueeraj@gmail.com, mdabdulmalekfahim@gmail.com.} \and Md.\ Abdul Malek Fahim}

\noindent{\small\textit{\textbf{Abstract:} Simulation records for CsPbI3 solar cells now exceed the certified experimental frontier (22.02\%), but the numbers rest on undisclosed assumptions. We screen an ITO/TiO2/CsPbI3/CBTS/Ni cell in SCAPS-1D over a stated guardrailed box---absorber 0.4--2.2~$\mu$m, $N_A$ $10^{15}$--$3\times10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$, $N_t$ $10^{12}$--$10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$, ETL $N_D$ $10^{16}$--$10^{19}$~cm$^{-3}$, $E_g$ 1.65--1.75~eV with linked affinity, interfaces $10^{10}$--$10^{12}$~cm$^{-2}$ (a $10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$ floor, i.e.\ $S=100$~cm/s, is part of the box; runs below it are audit only)---and price every assumption with computed sweeps. The best evaluated guardrailed point reaches 24.95\% (Voc 1.321~V, Jsc 21.20~mA/cm$^2$, FF 89.11\%) at joint affinities $\chi_{\mathrm{CBTS}}=3.9$/$\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}=3.7$~eV; a 104-configuration optimiser over the box peaks at 23.08\%, below all grid champions. A detailed-balance Voc computed from the model's own absorption (1.371~V at 1.65~eV) leaves the champion a 0.05~V margin and puts the top no-interface cell above the radiative limit with the rest inside 0.011~V of it---the band has no margin anywhere. Derated comparators at the same base give 24.44--24.73\% at attainable gaps ($E_g=1.68$--1.70~eV) and 24.34\% with $R_s=1~\Omega$cm$^2$ at $E_g=1.70$~eV; at routine defects the model gives \textbf{20.82\%}, 20.42\% with $R_s=1$. A paired-trajectory Morris analysis favours interfaces over bulk defects by 2.03 points (95\% CI [0.70, 3.51]) at the defect floor, while the same dose--response goes nearly flat at routine defects---so the ranking is regime-dependent, not universal. All definition files, sweep receipts, and raw curves are archived in the public repository for independent reproduction.}}

\medskip
\noindent{\small\textbf{Keywords:} CsPbI3; perovskite solar cell; SCAPS-1D; CBTS; reproducibility; device simulation}

\section{Introduction}

All-inorganic CsPbI3 perovskite solar cells combine the thermal stability lacking in hybrid organic--inorganic perovskites with a bandgap near 1.7~eV that suits both single-junction and tandem top-cell applications~\cite{Dai2026,Qiu2025}. After years below 19\%, certified laboratory efficiencies have recently passed 22\%: 22.02\% certified (22.60\% laboratory) with a moisture-responsive propyltriethoxysilane crystallisation strategy~\cite{Dai2026}, 22.05\% by fluorination-assisted interfacial dipole engineering~\cite{Qiu2025}, 21.71\% with dual-interface and bulk co-passivation at an open-circuit voltage of 1.27~V~\cite{Zhang2026}, and 21.43\% certified for inverted architectures~\cite{Joule2026}. Each record was won at the interfaces and in the bulk defect chemistry, which motivates a simulation study that treats those exact levers honestly.

The one-dimensional solar cell capacitance simulator (SCAPS-1D) is the workhorse for such pre-experimental screening, and the ITO/TiO2/CsPbI3/CBTS (copper barium thiostannate) stack of \citet{Hossain2023} is the most-prescribed CsPbI3 baseline, progressing from 17.90\% over 96 screened transport-layer combinations~\cite{Hossain2022} to 19.06\% after optimisation. Subsequent simulation studies report up to 24.17\% on the same stack~\cite{Nazli2025} and 24.24\% on ZnO/PTAA~\cite{Oyedele2023}, while large machine-learning-coupled screens now exceed 27\% on other absorbers~\cite{PerovskiteOpt2026,Bifacial2026}. Three problems accompany this inflation. First, nearly every study optimises one variable at a time (OVAT), so parameter interactions---notably absorber thickness versus defect-limited diffusion length---are invisible by construction. Second, the highest numbers are obtained with interface recombination removed (stated explicitly in~\cite{Oyedele2023}) or with defect densities far below experimental reach, and raw data are routinely withheld~\cite{Hossain2023}---we report our own data the same critical way, and where we could not reproduce others for lack of published parameters, we say so instead of inferring inflation. Third, scripted sweeps mix unit systems: SCAPS definition files store SI units while script `set' commands expect practical units, so SI-valued inputs silently inject a $10^6\times$ overdose and fabricate ghost cells (scripting conventions are documented in Appendix~A).

This work contributes (i) a five-factor grid screen (96 configurations) plus refinement (36 runs) of the ITO/TiO2/CsPbI3/CBTS/Ni cell under interface-inclusive guardrails, with a joint ETL/HTL-affinity map (36 runs) locating the best evaluated guardrailed point at \textbf{24.95\%} ($\chi_{\mathrm{CBTS}}=3.9$/$\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}=3.7$~eV); a 104-configuration optimiser over the declared box peaks at 23.08\%, below every grid champion; (ii) an interface dose--response computed on our own cell, reported in bulk lifetime $\tau$ and interface velocity $S$ alongside raw densities; (iii) scripted (not analytic) series- and shunt-resistance accounting, including the routine-defect case; and (iv) a Morris sensitivity screen with a paired-trajectory bootstrap, reported with explicit range-dependence. Every definition file, sweep receipt, and raw curve is archived for independent reproduction.


\section{Literature: a decade of CsPbI3 progress}

\sloppy
Black-phase CsPbI3 has been stabilised stepwise since 2016: quantum-dot-induced $\alpha$-phase retention at 10.8\%~\cite{Swarnkar2016}, co-evaporated planar cells at 17.0\%~\cite{Frolova2017}, thermodynamically stable $\gamma$-films~\cite{Zhao2018}, graded-gap 14.4\% devices~\cite{Bian2018}, and compositionally engineered 13--14\% cells~\cite{Xi2019,Becker2019}, all on TiO2 with Spiro-OMeTAD, PTAA or carbon contacts~\cite{Luo2016,Ke2018,Xiang2018}. The 2019 aziridinium result at 18.40\%~\cite{Wang2019} stood for years until the 2025--2026 interface-engineering wave (Figure~\ref{fig:timeline}): fluorinated dipoles (22.05\%~\cite{Qiu2025}), dual-interface plus bulk co-passivation with Voc 1.27~V (21.71\%~\cite{Zhang2026}), moisture-responsive crystallisation (22.60\% laboratory, 22.02\% certified~\cite{Dai2026}), and stitched grain-boundary grooves in inverted cells (21.43\% certified~\cite{Joule2026}). The certified frontier is therefore 22.02\% (Dai; laboratory best 22.60\%; Qiu's 22.05\% is uncertified), and every recent jump came from defect and interface control---the precise levers a simulation study must treat honestly.

Simulation studies trace a parallel inflation curve (Table~\ref{tab:lit}). The CBTS screening programme reached 17.90\% over 96 transport-layer combinations~\cite{Hossain2022} and 19.06\% after full optimisation~\cite{Hossain2023}, the baseline we reproduce. Later claims diverge upward as realism constraints are relaxed: 23.10\% with ZnO/Spiro in one report~\cite{Ristiansyah2026}, 24.17\% on our exact stack~\cite{Nazli2025}, and 24.24\% on ZnO/PTAA without interface layers (stated)~\cite{Oyedele2023}. The broader SCAPS literature shows the same pattern across absorbers---MAPbI3 at 19.30\% with inorganic contacts~\cite{Son2024}, gradient-doped FAPbI3 at 20.34\%~\cite{Ritu2024}, a 28.38\% bifacial triple-cation cell~\cite{Bifacial2026}, and an explicitly idealised 40.17\% MASnI3 result that exceeds the Shockley--Queisser bound~\cite{MASnI3ML2026,SQ1961}. Section~11.0 states the common reporting standard these numbers would need as a concrete checklist---interface status with dose level, defect floors with cross-sections---and demonstrates it on our own cell, since the published parameter tables are too incomplete to re-place anyone else's.

\section{Simulation framework and guardrails}

Devices were simulated in SCAPS-1D v3.3.10 under AM1.5G illumination (100~mW/cm$^2$) at 300~K unless stated. The baseline reproduces \citet{Hossain2023}: ITO front contact (4.0~eV), 30~nm TiO2 electron transport layer (donor density $9\times10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$), CsPbI3 absorber (800~nm initial, $E_g=1.694$~eV, $\chi=3.95$~eV, $N_A=10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$, $N_t=10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$), 100~nm CBTS hole transport layer ($N_A=10^{18}$~cm$^{-3}$), and Ni back contact (5.5~eV). Crucially, neutral interface recombination blocks ($N=10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$, $\sigma=10^{-19}$~m$^2$) are present at both heterojunctions, and the absorber uses the coefficients-A-and-B absorption model ($A=10^7$~m$^{-1}$eV$^{-1/2}$) so that bandgap sweeps act on the absorption edge rather than a frozen file spectrum. Our unmodified baseline yields 18.99\% (Voc 1.122~V, Jsc 19.68~mA/cm$^2$, FF 86.00\%), reproducing the published 17.9--19.06\% band; against the printed 17.90\% device (Voc 0.997~V, Jsc 21.07~mA/cm$^2$, FF 85.21\%~\cite{Hossain2022}) ours trades $\sim$1.4~mA/cm$^2$ of current for $\sim$0.12~V of voltage, as expected from added interface recombination with lower bulk defects---a single-scalar match is not claimed as validation. Optical settings: the definition file applies a flat 10\% front reflection with no dispersive parasitic absorption in ITO or TiO2, and the 80\% back-transmission filter faces an opaque Ni contact, i.e.\ no back reflector---both choices are conservative-or-neutral for Jsc except in the blue, where the flat QE plateau is an upper envelope (Section~6.0).

Guardrails enforced throughout: bulk defect floor $10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ (single-crystal grade; nothing lower), absorber doping ceiling $3\times10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$, an interface floor of $10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$ that is part of the stated box rather than a post-hoc filter (dose points below it are audit, not candidates), conduction-band offset held near zero by linking $\chi$ to $E_g$ ($\chi=3.95+0.5(E_g-1.694)$), and two energetic screens applied on inspection: a run with Voc above the detailed-balance value computed from the model's own Eg-sqrt absorption (1.371~V at 1.65~eV with $A=10^7$~m$^{-1}$eV$^{-1/2}$ and 2.2~$\mu$m single-pass absorptance; the model sets $k_{rad}=0$) or FF above Green's ideal-diode value at the computed Voc (90.5\% at the joint optimum) would be discarded. Box constraints above are enforced per run by construction; these two energetic screens are \emph{not} wired into the batch scripts---no run in the archive was rejected by them---so they are an audit applied after the fact, and we say so rather than claim an automated gate. The $E_g/q-0.28$~V rule of earlier drafts is retired: it sat above the radiative limit and could not adjudicate anything. Series and shunt resistances are scriptable in SCAPS~3.3.10 (\texttt{set external.Rs/Rsh}; \texttt{scriptdescription3310.txt}), so this section reports computed parasitic sweeps. Sweeps ran in parallel on four workers with checkpointed receipts; of 132 grid configurations, 126 converged and enter the analysis (6 runs excluded and listed in the receipts: three Round-A runs---A010 (1.0~$\mu$m, $N_A=10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$, $N_t=10^{14}$, $E_g=1.694$~eV), A081 (2.0~$\mu$m, $N_A=10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$, $N_t=10^{14}$) and A051 (1.8~$\mu$m, $N_A=10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$, $N_t=10^{12}$)---and three Round-B runs, all at 1.8~$\mu$m thickness. All six are missing-result-file worker crashes, not solver divergence, and none is a top-ten entry; because they cluster at low $N_A$ we cannot rule out that region being harder to converge, and we note it rather than claim the exclusions are unbiased. A duplicate champion run reproduces the coarse-grid value exactly, confirming determinism; a confirmatory run at finer IV step gives 23.4874\% at the surveyed affinity (FF 89.78\%) against its coarse partner 23.5041\%, a 0.017-point IV-step uncertainty against which all reported differences should be read. SCAPS batch scripts expose no mesh control, so no mesh-refinement study is possible in this harness; results are quoted to two decimals in the text (four only where digit-identical receipt comparisons require it). Absorber densities of states are capped at $N_c=1.1\times10^{19}$/$N_v=8.2\times10^{19}$~cm$^{-3}$, ten times below the source paper's Table~1 print ($10^{20}$~cm$^{-3}$, above solid density and hence unphysical).


SCAPS-1D solves the Poisson equation coupled to electron and hole continuity with drift-diffusion transport~\cite{Khattak2019,BurgelmanSCAPS}:
\begin{equation}
-\frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(\varepsilon(x)\frac{\partial V}{\partial x}\right) = q[p-n+N_D^+-N_A^-+p_t-n_t],
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\frac{\partial n}{\partial t}=\frac{1}{q}\frac{\partial J_n}{\partial x}+G_n-R_n,\quad
\frac{\partial p}{\partial t}=-\frac{1}{q}\frac{\partial J_p}{\partial x}+G_p-R_p,
\end{equation}
with Shockley--Read--Hall recombination through the specified bulk and interface defect levels. Optical generation uses the Eg-sqrt (Tauc) model $\alpha=A\sqrt{h\nu-E_g}$, so bandgap sweeps move the absorption edge self-consistently. Full input parameters are listed in Tables~\ref{tab:in} and~\ref{tab:if}, with every guardrail and its justification in Table~\ref{tab:guard}; transport-layer screenings that motivate the TiO2/CBTS choice are reviewed in~\cite{Hossain2022,Raoui2019}.

\section{Grid screen and joint-optimum champion}

Round~A explored the full cross-product of absorber thickness (1.0--2.0~$\mu$m), acceptor density ($10^{15}$--$10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$), bulk defect density ($10^{12}$--$10^{14}$~cm$^{-3}$), ETL donor density ($9\times10^{16}$--$9\times10^{17}$~cm$^{-3}$), and bandgap (1.694/1.65~eV with linked affinity)---96 configurations in a single parallel batch, rather than sequential OVAT slices. The winner (2.0~$\mu$m, $N_A=10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$, $N_t=10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$, $N_{D,ETL}=9\times10^{17}$~cm$^{-3}$, $E_g=1.65$~eV) reached 23.47\%. Full parameters are collected in Table~\ref{tab:champ}. Round~B refined thickness (1.8--2.2~$\mu$m), gap (1.65--1.72~eV), and doping around this point (36 configurations) and reached 23.50\% (2.2~$\mu$m, $N_A=3\times10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$, $N_t=10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$, $E_g=1.65$~eV, $\chi=3.928$~eV). A subsequent ETL-affinity sweep showed the surveyed 4.0~eV is not optimal: 3.9~eV gives 23.80\%, 3.8~eV gives 23.82--23.84\% across two batches (23.8241 in \texttt{s7\_r3} and \texttt{s11}, 23.8365 in \texttt{s8}; the 0.012 spread is inside the 0.017-point IV-step uncertainty above, and we quote 23.84\% for the batch that produced the gap-step and $E_t$ analysis, against the surveyed anchor $23.5041$), while 4.1 and 4.2~eV collapse to 21.92\% and 19.87\%. Because the two affinities interact through the interface activation energy, we then mapped them jointly at guardrailed interfaces (Table~\ref{tab:chia}, 36 runs): at fixed $\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}$, efficiency rises monotonically with $\chi_{\mathrm{CBTS}}$ through 3.90~eV, and the peak extension (3.95--4.10~eV) turns over past $\sim$3.95~eV, so the optimum is interior, not edge-sitting. The best evaluated guardrailed point is \textbf{24.95\%} at $\chi_{\mathrm{CBTS}}=3.9$/$\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}=3.7$~eV (Voc 1.321~V, Jsc 21.20~mA/cm$^2$, FF 89.11\%; Figure~\ref{fig:jvboth}), verified digit-identical with explicitly set $N_{if}=10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$ and falling to 24.24\% at $10^{11}$~cm$^{-2}$, confirming the interfaces are active at the optimum. A 104-configuration optimiser (LHS plus pattern search over thickness, $\log N_A$, $\log N_t$, $\log N_D$, $E_g$, $\log N_{if}$, $\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}$) peaks at 23.08\% under the guardrail---below every grid champion---so 24.95\% stands as the best of $\sim$350 evaluated guardrailed configurations, not as a proven global optimum. Two features of this point matter. First, it sits at the corner of the allowed box in every dimension except the affinities, which are themselves aggressive ($\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}=3.7$~eV below the typical 4.0--4.2~eV range; $\chi_{\mathrm{CBTS}}=3.9$~eV above the surveyed 3.6~eV): this is a permissive-edge upper bound, and Section~9.0 prices each edge. Second, the best grid point at the literature gap $E_g=1.694$~eV reaches 22.506\%, coincidentally equal at two decimals to the 22.514\% of the $E_g=1.70$~eV attainable-gap run on a different geometry (they differ by 0.008 points, inside step uncertainty), so roughly one point comes from the gap choice alone. Every top-ten configuration carries $E_g=1.65$~eV, gaining $\sim$1.5~mA/cm$^2$ over 1.694~eV; the joint optimum presents a $+0.23$~eV ETL-side electron spike that raises the interface recombination activation energy (Section~5.0).

From diffusion estimates ($\mu_n=25$~cm$^2$/Vs, $\sigma=10^{-19}$~m$^2$): $L\approx80$~$\mu$m at $10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$, $\approx$8~$\mu$m at $10^{14}$~cm$^{-3}$, $\approx$2.5~$\mu$m at $10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$. The map (Figure~\ref{fig:contour}) is therefore nearly thickness-insensitive at $10^{14}$~cm$^{-3}$ (near-vertical contours)---a thickness collapse there cannot be diffusion-limited, so we do not claim one. The genuine thickness--defect interaction appears at $10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$, where a dedicated sweep gives 20.06\% (0.5~$\mu$m), 20.72\% (0.8~$\mu$m), 20.82\% (1.0~$\mu$m), 20.77\% (1.5~$\mu$m): thickness matters exactly where $L$ approaches the film, which single-variable sweeps at fixed defect levels cannot resolve. ETL donor density confirms the literature optimum ($9\times10^{17}$~cm$^{-3}$) and transport-layer thicknesses are insensitive (100/30~nm retained), both consistent with~\cite{Hossain2023}. The current--voltage curve (Figure~\ref{fig:jvboth}) is square and artefact-free, with a Voc deficit of 0.40~V against $E_g/q$.

The 5.96-point stacked gain decomposes along the screening path (Table~\ref{tab:champ} parameters in sequence, illustrative ordering only): thickness 800~nm to 1.5~$\mu$m adds 0.19 points (19.18\%), acceptor doping to $10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$ adds 0.93 points (20.11\%), bulk-defect reduction to $10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ adds $\sim$1.6 points ($\sim$21.7\%), the joint $E_g$--$\chi$ move to 1.65~eV with ETL donor optimisation contributes $\sim$1.8 points (to the 23.50\% surveyed best), and the joint affinity optimum adds the final 1.45 points (modulo rounding). This sequential attribution is order-dependent and illustrative, not causal. Open-circuit voltage climbs 1.122 to 1.321~V while the fill factor rises 86.0 to 89.1\%, the signature of SRH-lifetime recovery plus interface-activation recovery rather than band-shift artefacts.

\section{Band alignment}

Figure~\ref{fig:align} constructs the equilibrium alignment from the joint-optimum parameters. The absorber conduction edge ($-3.928$~eV) lies 0.23~eV \textit{below} the TiO2 edge ($-3.70$~eV), so electrons face a spike entering the ETL. The data support reading this as recombination physics, not transport: the interface recombination activation energy $E_a=E_{c,\mathrm{abs}}-E_{v,\mathrm{HTL}}$ grows from 1.47~eV at $\chi_{\mathrm{CBTS}}=3.5$ to 1.87~eV at 3.9~eV, and efficiency rises monotonically through zero hole-side offset (22.10\% to 24.95\% at $\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}=3.7$; Table~\ref{tab:chia})---a transport reading predicts the barrier end should be worst, and it is the best. On the hole side, the absorber valence edge ($-5.578$~eV) lies 0.22~eV \textit{above} the CBTS edge ($-5.80$~eV) at the optimum, past the ideal $-0.3$ to $-0.1$~eV window on the barrier side---yet efficiency peaks there, which a transport reading cannot produce. The same activation logic applies to the ETL side, which is why the spike buys rather than costs efficiency. Both optimum affinities sit outside the surveyed values ($\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}=3.7$ below the typical 4.0--4.2~eV; $\chi_{\mathrm{CBTS}}=3.9$ above the surveyed 3.6~eV) and are reported as joint-optimum adoptions priced in Section~9.0, not surveyed values.

\section{Device characterisation}

The quantum efficiency (Figure~\ref{fig:qe}) is flat at $\sim$89--90\% from 300~nm with the absorption edge red-shifted from 731~nm (baseline, 1.694~eV) to 752~nm (champion, 1.65~eV), directly explaining the Jsc gain. The UV plateau assumes the definition file's flat 10\% front reflection with no dispersive parasitic absorption in ITO or TiO2, so it is an upper envelope in the blue rather than a prediction; with TiO2 absorbing above 3.2~eV, of order 1~mA/cm$^2$ of the reported Jsc is at stake in the UV, which is large next to the points debated here and is stated as an uncertainty, not corrected. Integrating the computed QE against the AM1.5G spectrum gives 22.39~mA/cm$^2$ against the 21.20~mA/cm$^2$ IV value; the 1.19~mA/cm$^2$ gap is carried as Jsc uncertainty with the conservative IV value headlined. Capacitance--voltage analysis at 1~MHz (Figure~\ref{fig:cv}) shows rising capacitance with forward bias (31 to 39~nF/cm$^2$ over 0--0.5~V). The low-bias $1/C^2$ branch is linear ($R^2=1.000$) with the normal sign for a p-type absorber; its slope gives $N_A=2.93\times10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$, essentially the $3\times10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$ input, extrapolating to $V_{bi}=1.30$~V---a solver self-consistency check on the doping from its own electrostatics, not an independent validation. The SCAPS-extracted width (0.29 to 0.22~$\mu$m) sits an order of magnitude below the 2.2~$\mu$m absorber throughout (the parallel-plate check gives 0.17~$\mu$m at 0~V, consistent in order with extra deep-level capacitance unaccounted). The illuminated band diagram at short circuit (Figure~\ref{fig:eb}) exhibits clean quasi-Fermi splitting, and generation exceeds recombination by at least two orders of magnitude at every mesh point of the full 2.33~$\mu$m short-circuit profile (minimum ratio $\sim$3$\times10^2$ at $x\approx0.2$~$\mu$m near the back contact, rising above $10^4$ at both contacts; Figure~\ref{fig:gr}). All profile statements in this section are at short circuit; nothing here constrains the maximum-power or open-circuit regime.

Temperature dependence (Figure~\ref{fig:t}, Table~\ref{tab:temp}) follows the established trend~\cite{Hossain2023}: efficiency falls from 25.88\% at 275~K to 18.13\% at 475~K, driven by Voc (1.357 to 1.038~V) and FF while Jsc stays pinned at $\sim$21.20~mA/cm$^2$, i.e.\ $-0.16$\%/K relative ($-0.039$ points/K) over the 300--475~K span. The 275~K fill factor (89.96\%) sits \textit{below} Green's ideal-diode value at that Voc and temperature ($\sim$91.4\%), so no artefact needs invoking; likewise the joint optimum's 89.11\% is about 1.4 points below ideal (90.5\%), leaving genuine FF headroom short of series resistance. The 275~K Voc (1.357~V) sits under the 275~K radiative limit (1.397~V, recomputed at that temperature), so the screen holds across the sweep. The 475~K end of the sweep ignores the temperature dependence of $E_g$ and black-phase stability, so it is a solver stress test, not a prediction.

\subsection{Parasitic-resistance accounting}

\sloppy
Series and shunt resistances are scriptable in SCAPS~3.3.10 (\texttt{set external.Rs/Rsh}; \texttt{scriptdescription3310.txt}). Computed scripted sweeps at the joint-optimum base give 24.73\% at $R_s=0.5~\Omega$cm$^2$, \textbf{24.52\%} at $R_s=1~\Omega$cm$^2$, and 24.09\% at $R_s=2~\Omega$cm$^2$ (Table~\ref{tab:rs}); a lumped-series analytic derate $\eta=\eta_0/[1+J_{sc}R_s/(FF_0V_{oc})]$, evaluated with the same unit convention SCAPS uses ($J_{sc}R_s$ in mV), tracks the computed sweep to within 0.011 points at all three $R_s$. Shunt paths cost 0.14 points at $R_{sh}=10^4~\Omega$cm$^2$ at the prior base; combined $R_s=1$/$R_{sh}=10^4$ at the joint optimum gives 24.38\%. The best point therefore survives parasitics, but only just: at $R_s=2~\Omega$cm$^2$ the margin over the 22.02\% certified record is about two points. At routine defects $R_s=1$ costs 0.40 points (20.82 to 20.42\%).

\section{Interface dose--response and the limits of auditing others}

Deleting the interface blocks (audit pairs in Table~\ref{tab:audit}, dose--response plotted in Figure~\ref{fig:audit}) inflates efficiency by 1.26--1.66 points absolute at the surveyed base (23.40 to 24.87\%, 23.47 to 24.73\%, 23.50 to 25.16\%), almost entirely through a 0.13~V Voc rise as interface recombination vanishes. But the binary ON/OFF comparison understates the audit: the full dose--response at the prior adopted base (Table~\ref{tab:ifdose}) runs 25.11\% at $10^8$~cm$^{-2}$, 24.77\% at $10^9$~cm$^{-2}$, 23.84\% at the $10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$ guardrail, 22.62\% at $10^{11}$~cm$^{-2}$, and 21.20\% at $10^{12}$~cm$^{-2}$. Because interface density and cross-section enter only as the product $N\sigma$, Table~\ref{tab:taus} restates the guardrailed regime in the portable metrics other studies can compare against: bulk lifetime $\tau=1/(\sigma v_{th}N_t)$ and interface velocity $S=\sigma v_{th}N_{if}$ (with $v_{th}=10^5$~m/s). Our guardrail is $\tau=100$~$\mu$s with $S=100$~cm/s. The decisive screen, however, is energetic, not parametric: the detailed-balance Voc computed from the model's own Eg-sqrt absorption is 1.371~V at 1.65~eV (1.418~V at 1.70~eV), and the no-interface cells we computed (1.363--1.382~V) sit within 0.011~V of that radiative limit---the top one above it, the rest with no margin either---because with $k_{rad}=0$ in the model there is nothing to hold the quasi-Fermi splitting below the radiative bound. A band that hugs the limit is not evidence of a working cell. The published 24.17\%~\cite{Nazli2025} and 24.24\%~\cite{Oyedele2023} values are therefore not placed on our curve at all: their stacks, gaps, thicknesses and defect parameters all differ from ours, neither paper prints a complete parameter table from which $\tau$ or $S$ could be reconstructed, and we state this as a limitation rather than a finding.

\subsection{Where the missing points go}

The inflation is almost entirely a Voc effect ($+$0.13~V at the champion cell, $+0.148$~V at 1.5~$\mu$m) with Jsc unchanged to within 0.02~mA/cm$^2$: removing the $10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$ interface states eliminates the dominant SRH channel at the heterojunctions, unpinning the quasi-Fermi splitting. The no-interface Voc values (1.363--1.382~V) all sit within 0.011~V of the 1.371~V detailed-balance limit computed from the model's own absorption, the top one above it: with $k_{rad}=0$ there is no radiative channel to pin the splitting, so none of these cells carries margin and none is trusted, regardless of rank order. Fill factor moves non-monotonically (89.86\% down to 85.3--87.1\% across the three audited cells) as the recombination profile reshapes. The no-interface 87.05\% at Voc 1.363~V sits 3.7 points below Green's ideal (90.8\%): the archived JV curve stays flat to 1.16~V with no kink or S-shape, so there is no visible extraction barrier, but the knee remains SRH-rounded by the surviving bulk channel---removing interfaces unpins Voc without idealising the diode. This bounds the ``no extraction barriers'' claim to current collection, not to fill factor. Asymmetric tests show both heterojunctions matter: $10^{12}$~cm$^{-2}$ on the ETL side alone gives 21.35\%, on the HTL side alone 21.20\%. Raising the capture cross-section $10\times$ at fixed $N_{if}=10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$ gives 22.2108\%, digit-identical to the $N\times10$ run at the same base (both 22.2108; receipts in Table~\ref{tab:runs}): for the symmetric single level, rate scales exactly with the $N\sigma$ product. The same identity holds in the bulk: $\sigma\times10$ at the $N_t$ floor gives 23.2572\% (digit-identical to $N_t\times10$ at the same base, $=23.2572$; receipts in Table~\ref{tab:runs}), a 0.25-point cost against the surveyed 23.5041 anchor. (A first attempt via the script \texttt{set} key for $\sigma$ neutralised the interfaces instead of scaling them; only the verified definition-file variant is reported---see Appendix~A.) Bulk $N_t\times\sigma$ costs 0.25 points at the $10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ floor but 3.12 points at routine $10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$ (20.5603\% at matched $\sigma\times1$ geometry down to 17.4433\%), while $\sigma\times0.1$ at the floor gains only 0.03 points (23.53\%)---the floor is saturated.) The computed parasitic sweep at the adopted base is tabulated below.

\section{Morris sensitivity screening}

Grid methods with uneven ranges cannot rank physical importance, so we ran a Morris sensitivity screen instead: $r=8$ trajectories, $p=4$ levels, $k=6$ factors (absorber thickness, $\log N_A$, $\log N_t$, $\log N_{D,ETL}$, $E_g$ with the $\chi$ link applied deterministically, and $\log N_{if}$ tied on both interfaces), 56 fresh simulations, all converged, spanning 15.6--23.3\% (Table~\ref{tab:morris}, Figure~\ref{fig:morris}). Per decade, interface quality leads at 1.02 points (bootstrap 95\% CI [0.84, 1.22]) ahead of bulk defect density at 0.68 (CI [0.35, 0.99]). Because marginal intervals overlap, we ran the sharper paired test the design allows: the per-trajectory difference $|EE_{Nif}|-|EE_{Nt}|$ averages $+$2.03 points with a bootstrap 95\% CI of [0.70, 3.51] (6 of 8 trajectories positive)---interfaces genuinely lead \textit{within the defect-floor regime}. Per eV, bandgap moves 17.5 points; per $\mu$m, thickness 0.72. These per-unit numbers are not commensurable across units, the interface figure bundles both heterojunctions over a 4-decade range against 3 for bulk, and---crucially---the $E_g$ factor confounds gap with band offset, since the $\chi$ link assigns half of every gap step to the conduction band while Section~5.0 shows alignment alone moves efficiency by several points. The gap-step pattern betrays the confounding (all on the prior adopted base, 23.8365 anchor): 1.65 to 1.68~eV costs 1.13 points but 1.68 to 1.70~eV only 0.19 (and 1.70 to 1.72~eV costs 0.93), tracking the $E_a$ landscape rather than the absorption edge. On the joint-optimum base the same steps even change sign (24.44 to 24.73\% from 1.68 to 1.70~eV), confirming the steps map the activation landscape, not the gap. The random-forest/Saltelli corroboration ($S_T=0.52$ interfaces, 0.33 bulk, 0.24 $E_g$; OOB $R^2=0.93$) is reported with the caveat that it is \textit{not} independent evidence: the surrogate trains on all 190 standard-base runs including the Morris design itself, so its indices partly reflect the sampling design. The decisive test remains the dose--response repeated at routine defects: at $N_t=10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$ and 1.0~$\mu$m, $N_{if}$ 10$^9$--$10^{11}$~cm$^{-2}$ moves efficiency only from 20.84\% to 20.67\% (0.16 points over two decades), while the $N_t$ 10$^{14}$--$10^{15}$ step costs far more. At the defect floor interfaces dominate; at routine defects bulk defects do. Trap depth is a non-factor at this defect level: moving $E_t$ to 0.3 or 0.9~eV changes efficiency by at most 0.012 points (23.8259\% and 23.8241\% against 23.8365\%).

Interface-led sensitivity is consistent with passivation studies in which interface-adjacent defects gate the voltage~\cite{Li2018}, and with Bayesian optimisation on CsSnI3 where the optimal thickness likewise shifts with defect density~\cite{PerovskiteOpt2026}.







\section{Discussion}

Fabrication plausibility bounds the result, and the computed sweeps price each term. $N_A=3\times10^{16}$~cm$^{-3}$ is routinely achievable; $E_g=1.65$~eV sits below the $\sim$1.7~eV of the experimental records and contributes roughly one point (best 1.694~eV grid point: 22.506\%); $N_t=10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ demands near-single-crystal quality ($\tau_{\mathrm{SRH}}\approx100$~$\mu$s, Table~\ref{tab:taus}). The contacts are load-bearing. At the surveyed anchor Ni 5.5 to 5.2~eV costs nothing (23.5041 to 23.5039\%, the Ni 5.2 value reproduced digit-identically across two batches) while Ni 5.0~eV costs 0.25 points (23.2571\%); on the joint-optimum affinities the same Ni 5.0~eV choice instead collapses the cell to 15.63\% (Voc 1.01~V) against 18.83\% at Ni 5.2~eV---a back-contact barrier cliff, not a slope, so the back-contact tolerance window collapses as the bands shift with affinity. ITO 4.0 to 4.7~eV collapses the cell to 18.60\% (Voc 1.08~V)---SCAPS's thermionic-only contact boundary, so 4.0~eV is the edge of what this model tolerates rather than a typical ITO value; the routine-defect penalty is larger still, with ITO 4.4~eV costing 0.14 points at surveyed $\chi$ (20.82 to 20.68\%) but 2.73 points at adopted $\chi$ (20.84 to 18.11\%): the front-contact tolerance window itself shifts with ETL affinity (Table~\ref{tab:real}). Both optimum affinities are aggressive ($\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}=3.7$ below the typical 4.0--4.2~eV window; $\chi_{\mathrm{CBTS}}=3.9$ above the surveyed 3.6~eV) and move efficiency through the interface activation energy rather than transport (Table~\ref{tab:chia}). At routine settings the model gives 20.82\% (1.0~$\mu$m, $N_t=10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$, surveyed $\chi$), 20.68\% with ITO at 4.4~eV on the same base, 18.11\% when that ITO is combined with the adopted $\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}$, and 20.42\% with $R_s=1~\Omega$cm$^2$. Against experiment (Table~\ref{tab:loss}): 24.95\% exceeds the 22.02\% certified record by 2.93 points; the excess over the best measured devices comes mostly from fill factor ($\sim$89\% simulated against $\sim$83\% measured) and the low gap, not from voltage---our Voc deficit (0.33~V against $E_g/q$, 0.05~V against the radiative limit) is comparable to the 1.27--1.29~V record devices. With computed $R_s=1~\Omega$cm$^2$ (24.52\%) the margin is 2.50 points, and at attainable gaps on the joint-optimum base the model gives 24.44\% ($E_g=1.68$~eV), 24.73\% ($E_g=1.70$~eV) and 24.28\% ($E_g=1.72$~eV), with 24.34\% at $R_s=1~\Omega$cm$^2$ ($E_g=1.70$~eV; $\chi_{\mathrm{CBTS}}=3.9$/$\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}=3.7$, ITO 4.0~eV throughout). The non-monotonic 1.68-to-1.70 step ($+$0.29 points) is the $E_a$ confounding of Section~8.0, not an absorption effect. The result sits at about four-fifths of the $\sim$30--31\% Shockley--Queisser limit at 1.65~eV. A final calibration note: integrating the computed QE against the AM1.5G spectrum gives 22.39~mA/cm$^2$ against the 21.20~mA/cm$^2$ IV value---a 1.19~mA/cm$^2$ gap we report as Jsc uncertainty (headline Jsc uses the conservative IV value) alongside the $\sim$1~mA/cm$^2$ UV envelope.

\section{Limitations and outlook}

A laboratory translation would need, simultaneously: $\sim$1.0~$\mu$m CsPbI3 films at routine defect levels for the 20.82\% case (time-resolved photoluminescence verified), interface passivation toward $10^{10}$~cm$^{-2}$ following the fluorinated-dipole~\cite{Qiu2025} or dual-interface~\cite{Zhang2026} chemistries, a front contact near 4.0~eV, and $R_s\le1~\Omega$cm$^2$ (Table~\ref{tab:rs}). Not demonstrated here: 2.2~$\mu$m device-quality CsPbI3 at $N_t\sim10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$, and sputtered CBTS directly on CsPbI3 (CBTS typically requires high-temperature sulfurisation), for which we found no precedent---so this section is a requirements list, not a recipe. In-line controls, where applicable: QE edge at 752~nm (Figure~\ref{fig:qe}) and the $-0.16$\%/K temperature coefficient (Table~\ref{tab:temp}).

Five boundaries delimit this work. First, $N_t=10^{12}$~cm$^{-3}$ at 2.2~$\mu$m demands near-single-crystal films, and with the modelled $\sigma=10^{-19}$~m$^2$ implies $\tau_{\mathrm{SRH}}\approx100$~$\mu$s, one to two orders beyond the best reported perovskite films; at routine $10^{15}$~cm$^{-3}$ a dedicated sweep peaks at 20.82\% (1.0~$\mu$m), 20.68\% with ITO at 4.4~eV on the surveyed base, 18.11\% when that ITO meets the adopted $\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}$, and 20.42\% with $R_s=1~\Omega$cm$^2$. Second, the contacts (Ni 5.5~eV, ITO 4.0~eV), the joint-optimum affinities ($\chi_{\mathrm{CBTS}}=3.9$/$\chi_{\mathrm{TiO2}}=3.7$~eV, both outside surveyed/typical ranges), and the barrier-side hole offset (+0.22~eV) are permissive-edge stated-box choices, each priced in Section~9.0. Third, phase stability of black CsPbI3 against the yellow $\delta$-phase, ion migration, $E_g(T)$, and damp-heat degradation are outside SCAPS-1D steady-state scope and must be validated experimentally, following the passivation routes of~\cite{Qiu2025,Zhang2026,Dai2026}. Fourth, the grid is a screen plus a 104-configuration optimiser, not a proven global optimum: the best point sits at the corner of the allowed box, the optimiser peaks 1.87 points below it, and the leading cluster is numerically inseparable. Fifth, the single-junction ceiling ($\sim$30\% at 1.65~eV~\cite{SQ1961}) caps how far any interface-inclusive screening can go.

\section{Conclusion}

Grid screening under interface-inclusive guardrails finds a 24.95\%-efficient best point in the stated CsPbI3/CBTS box and 20.82\% at routine defect levels, with every load-bearing assumption priced by computed sweep: single-crystal-grade defects, a low gap, a work-function-tuned front contact, and joint affinity optimisation at aggressive values. A 104-configuration optimiser confirms the grid champion from below. The same campaign prices the routine-defect thickness optimum, shows the interface dose--response to be regime-dependent (leading at the defect floor by a paired 2.03 points, nearly flat at routine defects), replaces an analytic resistance derate with scripted parasitic sweeps, checks the doping by Mott--Schottky self-consistency, and bounds the result by a model-derived radiative Voc that leaves the no-interface band without margin. Table~\ref{tab:checklist} states the reporting standard as a concrete checklist. We recommend guardrailed reporting (interface status \textit{with} dose level and defect level, defect floors \textit{with} cross-sections, unit-system declaration, Rs basis, contact work functions, affinity choices) as a publication standard for SCAPS studies.

\section*{Appendix A: two scripting traps and a verification rule}

\emph{Unit trap.} SCAPS definition files store SI units (metres, m$^{-3}$, m$^2$/Vs) but script \texttt{set} commands expect practical units ($\mu$m, cm$^{-3}$, cm$^2$/Vs)---verified by dose--response: \texttt{set layer2.NA 1e15} reproduces the file baseline (stored $10^{21}$~m$^{-3}$) exactly, while SI-valued inputs (e.g. $10^{22}$) inject a $10^6\times$ overdose and yield degenerate ghost cells (Voc 1.47--1.53~V, FF 91--92\%, up to 27\%). Practical flags that catch them: Voc above the $E_g$-implied ceiling for the modelled gap, or FF above Green's ideal-diode value at the computed Voc.

\emph{Structural trap.} \texttt{set interface<n>.IFdefect<k>.capture\_cross\_section} does not adjust $\sigma$ in place; it appears to restructure the interface defect block, and in our hands it neutralised the addressed interfaces entirely (one interface: 23.8565\%; both interfaces: 25.1494\%, essentially the no-interface value). The definition-file route (rewriting \texttt{sigma\_nleft/\dots/pright}) reproduced the $N\times10$ result to four decimals, which the set-key route could not.

\emph{Rule.} For any parameter that changes a defect population, verify the applied value with a \texttt{get} of the same field in the same script and record the returned number in the run receipt; treat a result that moves efficiency in the wrong direction as a failed application, not a physical finding.
